Good App But 3 Different Prices For the Same Premium Package?. I feel like this is a cool app. The idea is nice, and I do like the information they provide based off which part of the menstrual cycle you’re in. I think tracking your cycle is great so you can see how your overall wellbeing is during different phases of the month.

When you first log in, you get a pop up after entering all the information needed before getting to the home screen. It gives a 7 Day trial offer, then after that it’s $29.99 yearly, basically $2.50/mo

After exiting out, I scroll down the main page a little bit and see another little pop up offer for a 7 Day trial, then $39.99 yearly (3.33/mo) I think “huh, that’s weird kinda”. But assumed it was a mistake. 

THEN I look at the bottom of my screen and see a limited time offer to subscribe now and they 62% off. $18.99/year ($1.58/mo) versus $49.99/year (4.17/mo) 

So at this point I’ve seen 3 different prices for the premium package within like a minute haha. Maybe they’ve lowered the premium package to make it more affordable though and the ads need updated though! So if that’s all I have to say about the app then I think it’s worth the download overall

Amazing + a few small things.. After quitting the birth control pill, I struggled learning how to move through the seasons of my cycle. I, like most women, are never really taught what goes on in our bodies and how to live in a way that honors them. This app has been so helpful and gentle in navigating the various things I might feel throughout my cycle and, unlike other cycling apps that just provide raw data, provides suggestions on things I can do, foods I can eat, and ways I can move my body to feel better.

The few things I noticed are:

1) some of the do/move/eat suggestions are repetitive I had to hide a bunch of them when I first opened the app because it’s a little overwhelming to see so many icons. Once I hid the ones that felt repetitive, it was much easier to digest. 

2) There are a few typos I noticed one under “Eat- High Fiber”. 

3) I would love to be able to sync my temperature to my oura ring someday! That’s the only thing keeping me on another tracking app.

Otherwise I love this app and think it’s totally worth the few bucks a month. The widgets are super helpful in reminding myself where I’m at while I’m still adjusting to my cycle again :) Thank you!

reviews.text:
Completely forgot that many women lose their periods. I was excited to use the app hoping to get some insight about the phases based on tracking symptoms over time or at least get information on each cycle while it could not determine my particular phase. Immediately ran into trouble because the first question is the start of your last menstrual cycle. No idea in the world. I’ve had an IUD for over 7 years. There is no way to bypass this question. Not even a button for I don’t know or I don’t get periods. 

I’m not asking for something that is so niche as to not have been included. Tens of thousands of women lose their periods on IUDs, with other forms of birth control, of for other health reasons. That doesn’t mean the phases disappear or that we don’t want access to the information. 

It’s just such an oversight to have to pick an exact date without a date drop down boxes or a calendar select. Scrolling through 7 years worth of singular days in a wheel when you can’t even see the year you’re in is simply not happening. I went back 2ish years (don’t even know how many because again you can’t see the year) before I gave up and picked a random date. Once I finally got through, there were no options to adjust or add symptoms to help it figure out the phase nor anywhere I could find with anything to read for information.
